## Abstract

This paper estimates hedonic price functions for Chilean fresh whole salmon and fresh salmon fillets using customs data for the period 2012–2025. Using the product description field in customs data, we identify size category, an attribute that is often among the most important. We show that average size premia are modest in general for fresh whole salmon with limited evidence of seasonal variation, but with significant heterogeneity across destination markets and monthly exporter-value quartiles.

For fresh fillets of salmon, the size-price relationship is stronger, with both significant discounts and premia across different size categories. We find that the relative size-price relationship exhibit some seasonal variation for whole salmon but no similar seasonal effects are found for fillets. Size premia also differ significantly across destination markets and exporter-value quartiles for both product forms. The results show that the value of different size categories for the two products of interest primarily depends on product form, destination markets and exporter scale, with more limited evidence of seasonal variation. Primary processing, such as filleting, may dampen seasonal demand volatility for product attributes, providing a more stable pricing structure compared to farmed whole fish.
